title: Epic: Comprehensive Testing Coverage for All Major Functionality
description:
## Problem

Search functionality is completely broken in the CLI app, but CI is green on main. This reveals critical gaps in the testing pyramid, particularly at the acceptance test level.

## Root Cause

Acceptance tests are not testing from the USER'S perspective. They must:
1. Build the actual binary (go build)
2. Execute as subprocess (exec.Command)
3. Check stdout/stderr/exit codes
4. NEVER import internal packages
5. Treat the app as a black box

## Testing Pyramid Requirements

### Unit Tests (many, fast, isolated)
- Test individual functions with mocks
- Cover edge cases, error handling
- Run with: go test ./...

### Component Integration Tests (fewer, real interactions)
- Test real components together (Connector + API)
- Use build tag: //go:build integration
- May require credentials/network

### Acceptance Tests (fewest, USER perspective)
- Test ACTUAL USER EXPERIENCE
- Build real binary, run with real args
- Check stdout/stderr/exit codes
- Use build tag: //go:build acceptance
- Run with: go test -tags=acceptance ./tests/acceptance/

## THE RULE
**If a human follows the README and gets an error, an acceptance test MUST catch it.**

## Scope

Cover ALL major documented functionality:
- search command (currently broken)
- config command
- version command
- Any other user-facing commands in README
- Error handling for bad inputs
- Exit codes for success/failure

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All README examples have corresponding acceptance tests
- [ ] Search functionality acceptance test exists and would catch current bug
- [ ] 100% line coverage on new code (per function)
- [ ] CI includes acceptance test run
- [ ] make test-acceptance target exists
- [ ] Documentation in README references make targets
close_reason: Closed

AI-assisted interactive walkthrough to obtain and configure OAuth credentials.

## How It Works

1. Start Claude Code with `claude --chrome` (gives Claude the browser tool to see pages and help you)

3. Claude guides you step-by-step, opening URLs, explaining what to click, answering questions

This is NOT automation — Claude is your interactive guide. You drive, Claude navigates.

```bash
claude --chrome
# Then say: "Help me set up Google OAuth credentials for pkb"
# Or for any future service: "Help me add Slack credentials to pkb"
```

- Formula template: `.beads/formulas/mol-obtain-secret.formula.json`
- Full guide: `docs/obtaining-secrets.md`

## What Claude Does at Each Step
- Opens the right URL in your browser
- Tells you exactly what to click and fill in
- Can see the page via `--chrome` if you get stuck
- Writes credentials to .env (you never have to edit files manually)
- Runs the auth flow and verifies everything works

title: Epic: Enable Live API and E2E Tests in All CI Runs
description:
## Problem

Live API tests and Playwright E2E tests are SKIPPED in most CI runs due to overly restrictive conditions.

**Evidence:** https://github.com/thewoolleyman/personal-knowledge-base/actions/runs/21610400777
- Event: workflow_dispatch (manual trigger)
- Branch: main
- Result: Live API Tests and Playwright E2E Tests both SKIPPED

## Root Cause

In .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml, both jobs have:
```yaml
if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
```

This means they:
- ❌ DON'T run on workflow_dispatch (manual triggers)
- ❌ DON'T run on pull requests
- ❌ DON'T run on any branch except main
- ✅ ONLY run on direct pushes to main

## Impact

- Tests are never validated before merging (PRs don't run them)
- Manual CI runs skip critical integration tests
- Regressions can be introduced without detection
- No way to verify tests work without pushing to main

## Required Changes

### 1. Fix Workflow Conditions (ci-cd.yml)

**live-tests job (lines 107-137):**
```yaml
# BEFORE:
if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'

# AFTER:
if: |
  github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 
  (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
```

**e2e-tests job (lines 139-194):**
```yaml
# Same change as above
```

### 2. Verify Required Secrets

Both jobs need these secrets configured in GitHub:
- PKB_TOKEN_JSON
- PKB_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
- PKB_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET

Action items:
- [ ] Verify all secrets exist in repo settings
- [ ] Document secret setup in CI docs
- [ ] Add graceful failure if secrets missing

### 3. Consider Pull Request Execution

**Options:**
1. Run on all PRs (requires secrets in repo, not fork PRs)
2. Run only on PRs from same repo (not forks)
3. Add manual approval for PR runs
4. Keep main-only but allow workflow_dispatch

**Recommendation:** Start with workflow_dispatch support, evaluate PR runs separately.

### 4. Validate Tests Can Run

Before closing this epic, must:
- [ ] Trigger manual workflow_dispatch run
- [ ] Verify live-tests job executes (not skipped)
- [ ] Verify e2e-tests job executes (not skipped)
- [ ] Both jobs must pass (green)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] workflow_dispatch triggers run live-tests
- [ ] workflow_dispatch triggers run e2e-tests
- [ ] All required secrets documented
- [ ] At least one successful manual run with both tests passing
- [ ] Document when tests run (push vs dispatch vs PR)

## Security Considerations

- Secrets must NEVER be exposed to fork PRs
- Consider using environment protection rules
- Document secret rotation procedure

## Related

- Depends on secrets being properly configured
- May need credentials refresh if tests fail
- Consider adding test data fixtures to reduce credential dependence
notes: Created after discovering workflow run 21610400777 skipped critical tests due to event_name condition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Epic: Mandate E2E Tests for All User-Facing Epic Completions
description:
## Problem

Epics can currently be closed without verifying that user-facing functionality has top-of-the-pyramid E2E/acceptance tests. This allowed the search functionality bug to slip through even though CI was green.

## Root Cause

No documented or enforced requirement that:
- New user-facing features must have acceptance tests
- Epics must verify test coverage before closing
- Agents must check for E2E tests during epic completion

## Solution

Create mandatory checkpoints in documentation, workflows, and prompts that REQUIRE E2E tests for any user-facing functionality before an epic can be closed.

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Update CLAUDE.md - Mandatory Testing Requirements

Add new section after the Testing Pyramid section (around line 140):

```markdown
### 🚨 EPIC COMPLETION REQUIREMENTS

**MANDATORY: Before closing ANY epic that adds or modifies user-facing functionality:**

1. **Acceptance Test Checklist:**
   - [ ] Acceptance tests exist for ALL new CLI commands
   - [ ] Acceptance tests exist for ALL new HTTP endpoints
   - [ ] Acceptance tests exist for ALL new UI features
   - [ ] Tests build real binary and execute as subprocess
   - [ ] Tests check stdout/stderr/exit codes (black box)
   - [ ] Tests NEVER import internal packages
   - [ ] Tests mirror what README instructs users to do

2. **Test Coverage Verification:**
   - [ ] Run: `go test -tags=acceptance -v ./tests/acceptance/`
   - [ ] All new functionality tests pass
   - [ ] Tests would catch regression if functionality broke

3. **Documentation Alignment:**
   - [ ] Every README example has corresponding acceptance test
   - [ ] Test names reference README sections
   - [ ] Failure messages guide users to documentation

**THE RULE:**
> If a human follows the README and gets an error, an acceptance test MUST exist that would have caught it before merge.

**NO EXCEPTIONS:** Epics cannot be closed without these checks. If acceptance tests are blocked by external dependencies, file a blocker bead.
```

### 2. Update docs/project-management.md

Add new section "Epic Completion Checklist":

```markdown
## Epic Completion Checklist

Before closing an epic with `bd close <id>`, verify:

### For ALL Epics:
- [ ] All child beads are closed
- [ ] No blocking dependencies remain
- [ ] CI is green on main
- [ ] Code is merged and deployed
- [ ] Documentation updated

### For User-Facing Features (MANDATORY):
- [ ] **Acceptance tests exist** (see Testing Pyramid in CLAUDE.md)
- [ ] Tests build real binary as subprocess
- [ ] Tests verify from user's perspective (black box)
- [ ] Tests mirror README examples
- [ ] Run `make test-accept` - all pass
- [ ] Manual verification: follow README steps yourself

### For Internal Refactors:
- [ ] Unit tests updated
- [ ] Integration tests if needed
- [ ] No user-facing behavior changed
- [ ] Performance benchmarks if applicable

### Red Flags That Require Acceptance Tests:
- Added new CLI command or flag
- Added new HTTP endpoint
- Changed CLI output format
- Modified error messages users see
- Updated README with new examples
- Fixed a bug a user reported

**If you can't write acceptance tests yet:**
1. File a blocker bead explaining why
2. Update epic description with blocker details
3. DO NOT close epic until blocker resolved
```

### 3. Create .beads/templates/EPIC_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.md

New file with template agents can reference:

```markdown
# Epic Completion Checklist

Epic ID: `________`  
Epic Title: `________`  
Completed By: `________`  
Date: `________`

## 1. Core Requirements
- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] CI green on main
- [ ] Code merged
- [ ] Documentation updated

## 2. User-Facing Functionality Check

**Does this epic add or modify user-facing features?**
- [ ] YES - Complete section 3 below (MANDATORY)
- [ ] NO - Skip to section 4

## 3. Acceptance Test Requirements (MANDATORY for user-facing)

### 3.1 Test Existence
- [ ] Acceptance tests written in `tests/acceptance/`
- [ ] Tests use `//go:build acceptance` tag
- [ ] Tests build real binary with `buildBinary(t)`
- [ ] Tests execute as subprocess with `exec.Command`
- [ ] Tests verify stdout/stderr/exit codes
- [ ] Tests NEVER import `internal/*` packages

### 3.2 Test Coverage
- [ ] Every new CLI command has test: `TestAcceptance_<Command>*`
- [ ] Every new HTTP endpoint has test: `TestAcceptance_<Endpoint>*`
- [ ] Every README example has corresponding test
- [ ] Error cases tested (bad input, missing config, etc.)

### 3.3 Test Execution
Run and verify:
```bash
make test-accept
```
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] No tests skipped (unless documented)
- [ ] Tests would catch regression if feature broke

### 3.4 Manual Verification
- [ ] Followed README steps manually
- [ ] Built binary: `make build`
- [ ] Ran each new command
- [ ] Verified output matches expectations
- [ ] Checked error handling

## 4. Sign-off

I verify that:
- All checklist items above are complete
- If user-facing, acceptance tests exist and pass
- Epic can be safely closed

Signature: `________`  
Date: `________`

---

**IMPORTANT:** If any acceptance tests cannot be written yet, file a blocker bead and DO NOT close this epic.
```

### 4. Update Beads Workflow Context (.beads/PRIME.md)

Add to the "Session Close Protocol" section:

```markdown
## Epic Completion Protocol

**Before running `bd close <epic-id>`:**

1. Check epic type:
   - Feature/Enhancement with user-facing changes? → Requires acceptance tests
   - Bug fix for user-reported issue? → Requires acceptance test
   - Internal refactor with no user changes? → Unit tests sufficient

2. For user-facing epics:
   - [ ] Run: `make test-accept`
   - [ ] All tests pass
   - [ ] New functionality has test coverage
   - [ ] Tests verify from user perspective (black box)
   - [ ] Reference: .beads/templates/EPIC_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.md

3. For all epics:
   - [ ] CI green
   - [ ] All child beads closed
   - [ ] Documentation updated

**Agents: DO NOT close epics without this verification!**
```

### 5. Add CI Check (Optional - Follow-up Task)

Consider adding CI job that:
- Detects if acceptance tests were modified
- Requires acceptance tests for PRs with user-facing changes
- Comments on PRs missing acceptance tests

File as separate task: "Add CI check for acceptance test coverage"

## Success Criteria

- [ ] CLAUDE.md updated with epic completion requirements
- [ ] docs/project-management.md has epic checklist
- [ ] .beads/templates/EPIC_COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.md created
- [ ] .beads/PRIME.md updated with epic protocol
- [ ] Pattern stored in memory for future reference
- [ ] All documentation changes committed and pushed

## Validation

After implementation:
1. Close this epic using the new checklist
2. Verify checklist catches missing items
3. Update based on lessons learned
4. Store pattern in memory

## Related

- Blocks: Any future epics with user-facing features
- Related to: pkb-5vm (comprehensive testing coverage)
- Related to: pkb-b3g (CI test execution)

## Notes

This is a process improvement that prevents the class of bugs where:
- CI is green (unit tests pass with mocks)
- User-facing functionality is broken
- No acceptance test exists to catch it

The rule is simple: **If a user can trigger it, an acceptance test must verify it.**
notes: Process improvement to prevent user-facing bugs from slipping through CI with green status.
